title: Fraction Line Race
subject: math
goal: Place fractions on a number line, and find fractions that sit at the same point.
steps: Take turns. Roll two dice. The first die is the top number. The second die picks the bottom number (table below).
Find your fraction on the number line. Count the small marks: each whole is cut into 24 equal parts. Write your initials at that mark.
The Skeptic checks: how many marks is one part of your fraction? (For fourths, 6 marks.)
If someone's initials are already at that mark, you found an equal fraction: you both score a point. Example: 2/4 and 3/6 both sit at one half.
Past 2? It's off the line: pass. The Recorder writes every fraction and who scored.

dice.title: The second die picks the bottom number

listen_for: “Eighths are bigger than fourths because 8 is bigger than 4.” Ask: how many marks is one eighth? One fourth?
Counting tick marks from 1 instead of from 0.
Students explaining why 2/4 and 3/6 meet at the same mark.
debrief: List every pair of equal fractions the class found. Ask: what pattern do you see in the numbers?
Ask: which is bigger, 5/6 or 7/8? Use the line to show it.
sources: The idea is also modeled in PhET Interactive Simulations' Fractions and Number Line simulations (University of Colorado Boulder). The game and questions were written for Paper Loop.
